# A list const read by a state initializer, executed rather than read.
#
# A read of a list const is a reference to its declaration now rather than a
# literal copy, so the declaration has to exist before the first thing that
# reads it. On html that is the state object, which a page's script writes
# first, and the consts came after it: `shown` read `names` while it was
# still undefined, and the page threw before it rendered. A golden shows the
# order and only a browser shows what the order does, so this runs it; the
# other two runs are the same program on backends that bind a const before
# any state.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'


sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

const names = ["a", "b", "c"]

component main ui.node {
    var pick = 2
    var shown = names[pick]

    ui.text(value=shown)
}

func testReadsTheList(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.shown == "c")
}

ui.window {
    main
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/main/1 --

{
  "results": [
    {
      "Desc": "ReadsTheList",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
-- testrun/html/none/app.sngl/main/1 --
